We have been coming across various news reports regarding the gold 
loans and various practices adopted. Hence, we would like to spend 2, 
3 minutes on this to cover elaborately on such practices adopted by our 
bank, particularly on delinquency and LTV norms. Jewel loans are 
secured lending products, which is serving both agri and non-agri 
financing needs. 
 
Agri loan, which is income generation classification requires appropriate 
evidence of eligible underlying activity, while non-agricultural lending is 
completely a consumption purpose, which requires suitable purpose of 
end use. Bank prioritizes to maintain clear agri and non-agri based on

the purpose of the loan, documents evidencing the proof, proper credit 
assessments and the end-use control. This is aligned with RBI's revised 
lending against gold and silver collateral directions effective 1st April 
2026. 
 
In terms of LTV, under the RBI's harmonized directions applicable to 
banks from April 1, 2026. The earlier uniform 75% LTV cap has been 
replaced with a structure based on the loan amount and consumption 
loans. That is loan amount up to INR  2.5 lakhs, we can go up to 85% 
LTV, INR  2.5 lakhs to INR  5 lakhs, 80% LTV, above INR  5 lakhs is 
75% LTV. Please note, these are only maximum regulatory limits for 
consumption loans under the harmonized directions and not 
recommended lending targets. 
 
Generally, consumption loans are considered with the LTV range of 
60% to 65% at the time of on-boarding, though the permitted LTV is 
on the higher side and the daily LTV will be calculated on the last 30 
days average gold rate of India Bullion and Jewellers Association. 
 
While calculating the LTV on a day-to-day basis, the entire interest 
payable over the loan tenure up to the maturity to be considered 
upfront, along with the outstanding value of the account. So prior to 
the new regulatory guidelines, which is applicable from 1st April, the 
consumption loan will be classified as an NPA if the account reaches the 
threshold limit of 75%. 
 
However, as per the current regulation, when the LTV has breached the 
regulatory requirement, the bank has introduced the SMA flagging of 
accounts and the event of the breach of the prescribed LTV, the account 
will be classified as an NPA on 91st day. Generally, we keep 5% cushion 
for the margin call. That is 70% for the customers exposure above INR 
5 lakhs for the maturity balance -- above 5 lakhs, 75% for the maturity 
balance from INR  2.5 lakhs to INR  5 lakhs and 80% for INR  2.5 lakhs. 
 
As discussed, whenever the LTV has crossed, the entire list of accounts 
will be coming under the exceptional item of the client balance of the 
branches concerned for necessary follow-up. The customer is contacted
